instruction: Replace rejected first set. Reference actual LoL Volibear anatomy and StS2 native hand graphics; no modification of approved character or card assets.

pointing.art:
EDIT IMAGE 1, the actual Slay the Spire 2 Ironclad POINTING hand, into Volibear's POINTING claw. IMAGE 2 is the newly corrected Volibear PAPER sprite: match its exact character palette, matte painterly texture, gray-white long forearm, dark charcoal paw, cyan accents, and simple rendering. IMAGE 3 is Riot's original Volibear game model and controls anatomical details. Do not use any other previous image.
Only the index digit points straight upward; middle, ring and little digits are completely flexed inward into the paw; the short thumb closes low across the far side. Show the BACK of the pointing paw, matching image 1's orientation and knuckle arrangement. The ONE sharp claw tip reaches almost to the top; the pointing digit is thick and relatively short with an anatomically attached curved cyan talon.
Maintain exactly FOUR main short thick claw-bearing digits plus ONE low short side thumb. Compact bear paw structure, never long human fingers. Sharp curved muted cyan talons with simple turquoise edge, not glossy crystal jewels. Correct connected joints, no detached nails, no duplicated digits. Dorsal side faces the camera. No palm pads.
Use image 1's very tall 422:1200 native texture ratio and hand/long-forearm placement: paw within upper quarter, long continuous forearm occupying lower three quarters, entering from the bottom. Output 768x2184 or exactly that ratio, true transparent background. Keep forearm as close as possible to image 2, including silhouette and markings; only change the upper hand pose. Remove all Ironclad human skin, brass cuff, jewelry and brown fabric. Arm stays straight and nearly vertical with thumb on the LEFT.
STYLE: image 1's native StS2 graphic language and image 2's matching matte broad brushwork. Sparse fur tufts, 2-3 color planes, gentle irregular edges, almost no outline, no shiny highlights, no realistic strand-by-strand fur, no lightning glow. No letters, text, decoration or extra body parts.
pointing.layout:
Layout correction ONLY for this completed Volibear pointing hand sprite. Image 1 is the edit target. Image 2 is the native StS2 texture's required canvas and arm length. KEEP the anatomy, pose, all fingers, claw colors, hand size and painterly texture of image 1 unchanged. Match image 2's full tall canvas aspect ratio 422:1200 (about 1:2.84). The result must be a narrow TALL sprite, NOT the current wider 1:2.13 picture.
Extend the lower forearm downward, painting a continuation of its existing gray-white fur and sparse blue accents. Make the forearm longer by about 35 percent so the hand remains in the top quarter and the arm reaches the new bottom. Do not stretch or squeeze the hand or fingers to achieve this. Keep the original paw at the top. All extra area must come from new length of forearm below the wrist, not added empty transparent padding at the top. Preserve the thumb-left, hand-back-facing viewpoint and every visible digit.
Output portrait 768 x 2184 with a real transparent background. No background, no labels. Keep the fur matte and simply painted to match native StS2.

rock.art:
Correct ONLY the top hand pose in IMAGE 1. Preserve its canvas, transparent background, forearm, colors, painterly texture and long-arm silhouette exactly. Image 2 is the actual native StS2 closed ROCK fist pose to follow. Image 3 is official Volibear anatomy.
The mistake is that image 1 still shows five upward cyan claw tips like a half-open paw. Turn this into a FULLY CLOSED FIST viewed from the BACK. Flex every finger DOWN and IN at both finger joints. The top outline must be a rounded stepped row of four bare charcoal knuckles, like the native closed fist in image 2. All cyan claws are now on the hidden palm side, therefore NO cyan claws along the top outline. Hide the thumb claw too; the thumb folds across the hidden palm low on the left. Keep a broad compact bear fist, not a mitten, visible knuckle creases and believable short digits. No raised or extended finger, no extra digit. Do not repaint the forearm or introduce new fur details. Same soft matte brushwork as image 1.

paper.art:
EDIT IMAGE 1, the actual Slay the Spire 2 Ironclad PAPER hand texture, into Volibear's PAPER claw. IMAGE 2 is the official original-skin Volibear model: use its forepaw anatomy and colors. Preserve image 1's very tall 422:1200 canvas ratio, BACK-OF-HAND viewpoint, thumb-on-left orientation, gesture placement at the very top, and long forearm entering from the bottom. Output a portrait sprite at 768x2184 or the same aspect ratio, true transparency.
Replace the human hand with Volibear's broad charcoal-gray forepaw: four SHORT, THICK main digits and one lower lateral thumb/claw. All are extended in a loose open-paw PAPER gesture. Keep real bear knuckle structure, not human-length fingers. The claws are modest sharp curved dark-cyan talons with turquoise edges, attached at the digit ends as in the model; not big white crystal nails. We see the dorsal side: no palm pads. Replace the brass cuff and brown sleeve completely with ONE long white-gray furred forearm that darkens to charcoal near the paw, with just a few of Volibear's blue pointed accents. No bracer, clothing, human skin, gold, or jewelry. The paw occupies only the upper quarter; the long continuous forearm occupies the lower three quarters, matching the native sprite's proportions.
STRICT STYLE MATCH to image 1: simplified matte painterly brushwork, broad flat muted color areas, minimal outlines, slight coarse texture, 2 or 3 shadow values. No smooth shiny 3D shading, no intricate individual fur hairs, no anime highlights, no black comic-book outlines. The final image should look like it was painted by the same artist as the supplied StS2 hand, with Volibear's actual anatomy substituted. Keep everything else transparent.

continuity_pass.baseFade: Use case: precise-object-edit. Edit IMAGE 1 only, our Volibear pointing-hand game sprite. IMAGE 2 is the native StS2 Ironclad hand, reference only for how the lower arm ends. Preserve the pointing paw anatomy, its pose, silhouette, placement, dark-gray short fingers, cyan talon, forearm length, every fur tuft and blue accent of image 1. Do NOT redraw the paw or change the art style. Make ONE correction: the current lower arm ends in a visibly flat cut at the canvas bottom. In the bottom 12% of the image, gently taper the existing fur silhouette and fade its alpha into TRUE TRANSPARENCY, as a painterly UI sprite ending, so that the final 20 pixels are fully transparent and there is no hard horizontal bottom edge. This is not a detached limb end and not a white/black gradient background. The rest of the image must remain pixel-for-pixel unchanged. Keep the exact narrow tall original canvas ratio 422:1200 (744 x 2114 is fine); do not crop or stretch, do not add large padding or shift the hand. True RGBA transparent background throughout. No text.

gestureContinuity.rock:
Use case: precise-object-edit. Asset: native StS2 multiplayer Volibear hand sprite. Image 1 is the MASTER ARM and the only edit target. Image 2 is ONLY a reference for the upper finger gesture; DO NOT use its forearm, fur pattern, silhouette, blue accents, or bottom edge.
Change ONLY the fingers/knuckles within the top 30% of image 1 to: A FULLY CLOSED FIST seen from the BACK: all four short thick main digits bent completely inward and down; rounded charcoal knuckles form the top edge. The short thumb folds low across the hidden palm. All cyan claws are on the hidden palm side, so no upward claw tips. Match image 2's correct closed pose but fit it to image 1's wrist, without enlarging the fist.
MANDATORY LOCKED REGION: From 30% canvas height to the bottom, preserve image 1 PIXEL-FOR-PIXEL. Same arm width, exact same white/gray fur tufts, same blue crystal positions, same contours, same tapered alpha fade at bottom. Do not repaint this region; it must be exactly the same arm when the UI switches textures. Connect the new hand naturally at the same existing wrist. Keep image 1's existing dorsal orientation, matte native StS2 brushwork, muted colors, short thick LoL Volibear fingers. The four gestures belong to one animation, not four different arms.
Output same exact 744x2113 tall canvas/aspect 422:1200, true RGBA transparency. Do not stretch, crop, shift, or reframe. Keep all transparent empty space, preserve lower fade with alpha near zero at bottom. No background, no text, no new lights or details.
